title: Explore Unit Fractions as Part of a Set
goal: I can define a set as the whole and name one or more selected objects as a fraction of it.
catchAll: Name the whole set. Count every object for the denominator and the selected objects for the numerator.

teacher.def: The denominator of a fraction tells how many equal parts are in the whole. It is the bottom part of the fraction
A unit fraction is ONE part of a whole. It always has a numerator of one.
The numerator of a fraction tells how many equal parts are being described. It is the top part of the fraction.
A fraction is a number used when a whole is split into equal parts.

glossary.whole: the one shape, unit length, complete piece or entire set named in the question
glossary.partition: divide a whole into equal parts
glossary.interval: the distance between neighboring marks on a number line

screens.title: Name the whole
text: The entire collection is one whole set.

screens.title: Connect the parts
text: Each single object is one equal counting part of the set.
Name the whole set. Count every object for the denominator and the selected objects for the numerator.

screens.title: Check the reasoning
text: The selected objects need not be next to each other.

item.prompt: How is the whole in a fraction of a set different from a whole shape? Write a complete sentence.
item.example: For a set the whole is the entire collection of objects, while for a shape the whole is the area of one shape.
hints: Describe what the whole is and how its parts are counted.
show: Compare your reasoning with a grown-up or the model response.
For a set the whole is the entire collection of objects, while for a shape the whole is the area of one shape.

steps.say: The selected objects in the puzzle mat set are moved to new positions without adding or removing objects. Does their fraction of the set change?
Identify exactly what is being treated as one whole.
A fraction of a set depends on counts within the defined whole, not the objects’ positions.

sections.heading: What your child is learning
sections.text: I can define a set as the whole and name one or more selected objects as a fraction of it.

sections.heading: Ask for reasoning
list: How is the whole in a fraction of a set different from a whole shape?
What is the whole in this model? How do you know the parts are equal?
Can you explain the same idea with another picture or real objects?

sections.heading: Try it away from the screen
list: Put a few counters on a mat. Define all the counters as the whole set; move one aside and name its fraction.
Let your child explain a mistake before offering a correction.

sections.heading: Common mistakes
list: Counting unselected parts for the numerator or selected parts for the denominator.
Changing the whole halfway through a question.

sections.heading: About these questions
sections.text: These are original Study Scoop lessons aligned to the supplied chapter map. They are practice, not the teacher’s actual test. Written explanations are for comparison with a grown-up and are not automatically judged for mathematical meaning.
